jobs.occupation: Associate, GOglobal Graduate Program Inhouse Consulting (Trainee Program) (all genders) (Wirtschaftsingenieur/in)
jobs.description:
Work Your Magic with us!

Ready to explore, break barriers, and discover more? We know you’ve got big plans – so do we! Our colleagues across the globe love innovating with science and technology to enrich people’s lives with our solutions in Healthcare, Life Science, and Electronics. Together, we dream big and are passionate about caring for our rich mix of people, customers, patients, and planet. That's why we are always looking for curious minds that see themselves imagining the unimaginable with us.

Your role:

The GOglobal Graduate Program (GGP) is the company’s career accelerator for high potential graduates who are early in their careers. During the 24-month talent development program, you will gain experience through a combination of strategic management consulting projects and functional rotations tailored to your interests and development goals. These rotations may take place across Healthcare, Life Science, Electronics, and Group Functions.

In the first year, you will be working in the Inhouse Consulting team, where you will have the opportunity to tackle challenging problems under the guidance of experienced consultants and to acquire extensive management and problem-solving skills. Inhouse Consulting projects focus primarily on strategy, growth, as well as operational optimization, and our internal clients are typically senior-level executives within the company. The first year will help you to gain a good knowledge of the company and maximize your exposure to different subjects and stakeholders. You will also participate in targeted professional trainings as well as our coaching & mentoring program to continuously improve your technical expertise and business acumen.

In the second year, you will be working on several individual assignments within our sectors: Healthcare, Life Science, Electronics and Group Functions. Depending on our business needs and your preference, you’ll get the chance to expand your network and gain in-depth knowledge in the day-to-day operations of different functions, such as marketing, R&D, production, and strategic management. Each assignment will last three to four months, with one international assignment.

Overall, the program allows you to gain the skills and knowledge needed to become an early thought leader in an area, as well as the ability to independently manage complex projects and diverse stakeholders within a matrix organization.

After successful completion, you will move into an exciting role within one of our businesses depending upon your interest and career aspirations, professional development opportunities, and business needs from which you will continue your development as a future leader within the organization.

Next start date: March 2027, limited contract for two years; Position is based in Darmstadt, Germany with no support for relocation from outside Europe possible.

Several positions available

Who you are:

- Ideal candidates for the GOglobal Graduate Program are early in their careers (maximum 2 years of full ‑ time work experience), enjoy working in teams, and have a global mindset.
- MBA, Master’s degree, or PhD in natural sciences, engineering, or business.
- Candidates with an advanced degree in science or engineering must have demonstrated a strong interest in business through professional experience or internships in consulting or strategy in i ndustry ‑ related fields (e.g., pharma, biotech, diagnostics, bioprocessing, biology, chemistry, semiconductor solutions).
- Candidates with a business background must have demonstrated interest through professional experience, or internships in industry ‑ related fields (e.g., pharma, biotech, diagnostics, bioprocessing, biology, chemistry, semiconductor solutions) through relevant professional experience or internships.
- Practical experience applying Data & AI to solve business challenges in  industry ‑ related fields, combined with a passion for further developing skills in this area, is a plus.
- Strong analytical skills, excitement for complex and ambiguous work, curiosity for our diverse business sectors and a broad range of topics.
- Outstanding communication and team-work skills.
- Proactive and self-motivated mindset.
- Outstanding academic achievements.
- Profound knowledge of MS Office (especially Excel and PowerPoint).
- Excellent verbal and written English (German is a plus).

Recruiting Timeline:

CV Submission: By September 13, 2026 at the latest
Virtual Case Interview: Completed by the beginning of October 2026
Assessment Days on-site in Darmstadt:

- Option 1: Monday, October 12, 2026
- Option 2: Thursday, October 15, 2026
- Option 3: Monday, October 19, 2026

What we offer: We are curious minds that come from a broad range of backgrounds, perspectives, and life experiences. We believe that this variety drives excellence and innovation, strengthening our ability to lead in science and technology. We are committed to creating access and opportunities for all to develop and grow at your own pace. Join us in building a culture of inclusion and belonging that impacts millions and empowers everyone to work their magic and champion human progress!

Apply now and become a part of a team that is dedicated to Sparking Discovery and Elevating Humanity!

jobs.occupation: Master student in the field of Acoustics - Interior Noise (d/f/m) (Ingenieur/in - Luft- und Raumfahrttechnik)
jobs.description:
About us

Airbus pioneers sustainable aerospace for a safe and united world. The Company constantly innovates to provide efficient and technologically-advanced solutions in aerospace, defence, and connected services. In commercial aircraft, Airbus offers modern and fuel-efficient airliners and associated services. Airbus is also a European leader in defence and security and one of the world's leading space businesses. In helicopters, Airbus provides the most efficient civil and military rotorcraft solutions and services worldwide.
Job description

In order to support the Airbus Interior Noise department, Airbus Operations is looking for a

Master student in the field of Acoustics - Interior Noise (d/f/m)

You are looking for a master thesis and want to get to know the work of an Acoustics Engineer (d/f/m)? Then apply now! We look forward to you supporting us in the Interior Noise department as a master student (d/f/m)!

- Location: Hamburg
- Start: 01.01.2027
- Duration: 6 months

We are offering a Master Thesis opportunity focusing on acoustics, specifically interior noise. This role provides a unique chance to contribute to cutting-edge aerospace research and development within a leading global company.

Your location

You will be working at the largest production site for civil aircraft situated in Hamburg. Its location on the southern banks of the river Elbe includes the option to commute by ferry. Experience the special flair of Hamburg in your spare time where vibrant cosmopolitan culture meets nautic legacy.

Your benefits

- Work-life balance with a 35-hour week (flexitime).
- Mobile working after agreement with the department.
- International environment with the opportunity to network globally.
- Work with modern/diversified technologies.
- At Airbus, we see you as a valuable team member and you are not hired to brew coffee, instead you are in close contact with the interfaces and are part of our weekly team meetings.
- Opportunity to participate in the Generation Airbus Community to expand your own network.

Your tasks and responsibilities

- Conducting in-depth research and analysis of interior noise sources and propagation within aircraft cabins.
- Developing and applying advanced simulation models and experimental methodologies for acoustic analysis.
- Evaluating and comparing different noise reduction strategies and materials.* Collecting and analyzing data from various sources, including laboratory tests and flight measurements.
- Documenting research findings and presenting results in a clear and concise manner.
- Collaborating with experienced engineers and researchers within the acoustics department.

Desired skills and qualifications

- Currently enrolled in a Master's degree program in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Physics, Acoustics, or a related field.
- Strong academic record with a focus on acoustics, vibrations, or signal processing.
- Proficiency in relevant software tools (e.g., MATLAB, ANSYS, COMSOL, LMS Test.Lab) is a plus.
- Experience with experimental acoustics and data acquisition systems is beneficial.
- Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
- Fluency in English (written and spoken) is required; German language skills are a plus.

Please upload the following documents: cover letter, CV, relevant transcripts, enrollment certificate.

Not a 100% match? No worries! Airbus supports your personal growth.

Take your career to a new level and apply online (https://www.airbus.com/en/careers) now!

This job requires an awareness of any potential compliance risks and a commitment to act with integrity, as the foundation for the Company’s success, reputation and sustainable growth

By submitting your CV or application you are consenting to Airbus using and storing information about you for monitoring purposes relating to your application or future employment. This information will only be used by Airbus.
Airbus is committed to achieving workforce diversity and creating an inclusive working environment. We welcome all applications irrespective of social and cultural background, age, gender, disability, sexual orientation or religious belief.

At Airbus, we support you to work, connect and collaborate more easily and flexibly. Wherever possible, we foster flexible working arrangements to stimulate innovative thinking.

jobs.occupation: Global Head of Strategy & Real Estate (Fachwirt/in - Facility-Management)
jobs.description:
Work Your Magic with us!

Ready to explore, break barriers, and discover more? We know you’ve got big plans – so do we! Our colleagues across the globe love innovating with science and technology to enrich people’s lives with our solutions in Healthcare, Life Science, and Electronics. Together, we dream big and are passionate about caring for our rich mix of people, customers, patients, and planet. That's why we are always looking for curious minds that see themselves imagining the unimaginable with us.

This is one of the most strategically significant roles in the new CREM structure — and in many respects the strategic right hand of the Head of CREM. As Head of Strategy & Real Estate, you will build and lead the capability that connects Merck's business direction to its global real estate portfolio: translating corporate strategy into actionable portfolio plans, owning the business partnering relationships with sector leadership, and overseeing the execution of transactions across EMEA, AMER and APAC.
This is a newly created function. Portfolio strategy, proactive planning and workplace strategy do not currently exist in a mature form within Merck's real estate organisation — you will establish them. Transactions capability exists and is largely retained; your mandate is to elevate it from reactive execution to strategically-led delivery.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

- Portfolio Strategy: Lead the development and annual refresh of CREM's Real Estate Plan of Record — translating business growth, consolidation and transformation requirements into a multi-year portfolio strategy with clear priorities, scenarios and business cases. Own portfolio optimisation as the function's primary strategic output.
- Business Partnering: Serve as a senior strategic partner to business sector leads across Healthcare, Life Science and Electronics — embedding CRE into business planning cycles before decisions are made, not after. Build trusted relationships that position CREM as a value-creating partner.
- M&A Support – Lead on all aspects of Real Estate and FM due diligence to support Merck M&A activity, managing cross-border due diligence and master planning to capture portfolio synergies, mitigate risk, and prepare portfolio integration plan. Once M&A transaction is signed then lead the implementation of all portfolio and service delivery integration activities.
- Workplace & Occupancy Strategy: Own workplace and occupancy planning strategy at a global level — setting standards, guiding space utilisation principles and ensuring portfolio decisions reflect both business needs and efficiency targets.
- Market Intelligence: Oversee the function's market intelligence capability — leveraging external partners and broker relationships to ensure portfolio decisions are backed by real market insight, proactive lease expiry management and benchmarked market data.
- Transaction Oversight: Provide strategic direction and oversight to the regional Transaction Managers across EMEA, AMER and APAC — ensuring all transactions are strategy-led, governed consistently and executed to a high standard. Maintain sufficient transaction expertise to provide cover and resource flexibility where needed.
- Portfolio Management Oversight: Direct the regional Portfolio Managers in building and maintaining portfolio performance visibility, opportunity identification and Plan of Record delivery across all geographies.
- Governance & Process: Champion the adoption of CREM's transaction and strategy governance frameworks — ensuring compliance with playbooks, approval processes and decision rights across the team. Responsible for approving all global real estate transactions above approved thresholds
- Stakeholder Engagement: Represent CREM in cross-functional forums alongside the Head of CREM — including OLC engagement, sector strategy sessions and M&A workstreams where real estate input is required.

QUALIFICATIONS

- 12+ years in corporate real estate, with a strong track record in portfolio strategy, location strategy or strategic business partnering at a senior level within a large multinational
- Demonstrated experience developing and owning portfolio strategy — scenario planning, multi-year planning, lease expiry management, location strategy
- Strong commercial acumen with the ability to build and present compelling business cases to C-suite audiences
- Deep understanding of transaction management across leasehold and freehold assets; sufficient execution expertise to provide leadership continuity across the regional transaction teams
- Experience working in a matrixed, multi-sector corporate environment; comfortable navigating complex stakeholder landscapes
- Exceptional relationship builder — able to operate credibly at senior business and executive level
- Exposure to workplace strategy and occupancy planning advantageous
- Master's degree in Real Estate, Business Administration, Finance or a related field
- Fluency in English required; additional languages advantageous given global remit

jobs.description:

Our colleagues across the globe love innovating with science and technology to enrich people’s lives with our solutions in Healthcare, Life Science, and Electronics. Together, we dream big and are passionate about caring for our rich mix of people, customers, patients, and planet. That's why we are always looking for curious minds that see themselves imagining the unimaginable with us.

United As One for Patients, our purpose in Healthcare is to help create, improve and prolong lives. We develop medicines, intelligent devices and innovative technologies in therapeutic areas such as Oncology, Neurology and Fertility. Our teams work together across 6 continents with passion and relentless curiosity in order to help patients at every stage of life. Joining our Healthcare team is becoming part of a diverse, inclusive and flexible working culture, presenting great opportunities for personal development and career advancement across the globe.

As Head of HR Global Healthcare Operations, you will be the global strategic HR leader for an organization of approximately 7,500 employees across 20 sites, serving more than 100 million patients every day. You will partner with senior leaders across operations, manufacturing, supply network, engineering, technology, and EHS to shape the people agenda for a complex, globally regulated GxP/GMP environment.

jobs.description:
Work Your Magic with us!

Ready to explore, break barriers, and discover more? We know you’ve got big plans – so do we! One of the most operationally significant roles in the new CREM structure, the Global Head of Facilities Management is responsible for leading and transforming Merck's facilities and workplace management function across a global portfolio of 340+ locations and 4.3 million m² — encompassing offices, standalone labs, warehouses and selected soft services at manufacturing sites across more than 60 countries.
This is a dual-focus role requiring transformational vision and strict operational leadership. You will consolidate our existing FM foundation into a high-performing, data-informed ecosystem designed to minimise operational vulnerability. Through uniform service delivery standards and a consolidated regional IFM vendor model, you will drive process efficiency, strengthen risk controls, and unlock strategic business value across Merck's global footprint.
The scale of the people dimension alone is significant: this role leads a global FM organisation with a substantial team within CREM, with additional headcount transferring from business sectors as the expanded remit is stood up.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

- FM Strategy & Vision: Define and own the global FM strategy for CREM — establishing a unified vision, service delivery model and operating standards across all asset classes and geographies, aligned to Merck's broader corporate objectives.

- Stakeholder Engagement: Build trusted relationships with business sector leads, site managers and senior Merck stakeholders — positioning FM as a value-creating partner and ensuring the function is responsive to business needs.
- Operational Leadership: Ensure consistent, high-quality FM service delivery and drive operational excellence across the full portfolio by standardising service delivery and optimising facilities performance — maintaining service continuity throughout the transformation and holding Regional Heads accountable for operational performance within their geographies.

- Budget Authority: Hold direct budget authority for FM vendor contracts and operational spend across the full scope — managing significant global FM expenditure, driving cost efficiency and ensuring financial transparency across the function.
- Standards & Compliance: Establish and enforce binding global FM standards — covering vendor protocols, preventative maintenance schedules, H&S compliance, SLAs and performance penalties. Ensure consistent application across all geographies.
- Manufacturing FM: Oversee the delivery of selected soft FM services at manufacturing sites — working in close collaboration with the Quality & Compliance Lead to ensure service delivery meets the specific operational and regulatory requirements of Merck's manufacturing environments.

- People Management: Lead, develop and inspire a global FM organisation — including four Regional Heads and the Quality & Compliance Lead — through a period of significant organisational change, building a high-performance culture.

- Demonstrated track record of leading FM transformation — vendor consolidation, IFM implementation, service standardisation and organisational change at scale
- Direct experience managing global or regional IFM partner relationships at a senior level — contract negotiation, performance management and strategic vendor governance
- Strong financial acumen — experienced in holding direct budget authority for significant FM operational spend
- Exposure to regulated environments — life sciences, Good x Practice (GxP), pharmaceutical or chemical manufacturing — strongly preferred
- Exceptional people leader — able to lead a large, diverse and geographically dispersed organisation through transformation
- Data-driven approach to FM performance — familiar with CAFM/IWMS platforms, KPI frameworks and industry benchmarking standards

jobs.occupation: Verantwortliche Elektrofachkraft Offshore-Windkraftanlagen (m/f/d) (Techniker/in - Windenergietechnik/Bachelor Professional in Technik)
jobs.description:
Imagine a future where you play a key role in ensuring electrical safety across our offshore substations and wind turbines while helping us push the boundaries of safe, efficient, and reliable offshore operations.

Join us in this role where you’ll take independent ownership of electrical safety within your area of responsibility, overseeing electrical installations on wind turbines in our German wind farms. You’ll combine your deep technical expertise with on-site presence—both at your permanent base in Norddeich and offshore—in order to guide colleagues, strengthen procedures, and ensure safe systems of work.

Welcome to HV and Transmission GER

You’ll be part of HV and Transmission GER, where you and your colleagues will ensure electrical safety governance and operational support across high-voltage infrastructure in our German offshore wind farms. Your team is dedicated to managing safety-critical systems, uplifting operational standards, and sharing expertise across the organisation.

As a team, we collaborate closely, support one another’s development, and bring a proactive, solution-oriented mindset to every challenge.

You’ll play an important role in:

- preparing and reviewing risk assessments for offshore electrical work
- supporting the selection, training, and supervision of Authorised Persons, electricians, and electrically instructed persons offshore
- contributing to the qualification and supervision of contractors in the offshore electrical environment
- developing, implementing, and improving maintenance plans for offshore electrical installations
- coordinating multiple employers involved in offshore electrical activities
- planning, organising, delivering, and documenting electrical safety training
- implementing, strengthening, and regularly reviewing the Wind Turbine Safety Rules (WTSR) and Orsted Electrical Safety Rules (OESR)
- assuming designated roles within the Safe Systems of Work, such as Authorising Engineer, Authorising Officer, or Training Mentor
- auditing work processes before offshore deployment.

To succeed in the role, you:

- have completed a degree within electrical engineering, or equivalent
- bring strong expertise within electrical safety, including standards, laws, and regulations
- demonstrate technical leadership competence
- offer switching experience in high-voltage environments above 20 kV
- communicate confidently in both English and German at B2 level or higher
- are comfortable using IT systems, including Microsoft Office, SAP, and AI tools
- ideally have a qualification for live working, experience with wind turbines, or prior responsibility as an electrician
- meet the minimum competency requirements within your onboarding timeframe, supported by our learning and development processes.

**Country-specific requirements: **fulfil the requirements of a responsible electrician (vEFK) according to VDE 1000-10.

Please note that in this role you will be mainly working in our office in Norddeich from Monday to Friday. An important part of the role will be an inspection of plants and the professional guidance of the electricians. This requires partial work offshore (20-40%) in a 7- or 14-day shift pattern.

Maybe you’ve read the above and can see you have some transferable skills, even though they don’t quite match all the points. If you think you can bring something to the team, we still encourage you to apply.

Shape the future with us
Send your application to us as soon as possible. We’ll be conducting interviews on a continuous basis and reserve the right to take down the advert when we’ve found the right candidate.

As an applicant or employee, you may request reasonable work and position accommodation or adjustments via accommodation@orsted.com.
